mainTopic: The אשם מצורע and its נסכים, then the משנה about measuring vessels in the מקדש and whether their overflow is holy
overview: The amud opens by finishing the reason behind רבי יוחנן's ruling. A burnt offering spoiled for its original purpose can still become a voluntary עולה. There is no voluntary אשם, so an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו keeps its identity and still needs נסכים. A ברייתא backs him up. A new משנה then teaches that the measuring vessels in the מקדש were used heaped, except the כהן גדול's. It also teaches that overflow from liquid measures is holy, while overflow from dry measures is not, and רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי each give a different reason. The גמרא explains that the משנה follows רבי מאיר by reading 'all measures' as 'all measurings.' It then shows that the three views of the overflow rule differ over where each vessel was anointed. When the גמרא asks why overflow becomes holy without intent, רב says כלי שרת make things holy even without intent. רבינא answers instead that it is a rabbinic גזירה, and he defends that answer against רבי זירא's challenge from the לחם הפנים. Finally the גמרא starts defining מותר נסכים from a משנה in שקלים, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the אשם keeps its original status
steps.stepSummary: A burnt offering that no longer fits its original role can become a voluntary עולה. An אשם cannot, because there is no voluntary אשם, so it must stay what it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, if the burnt offerings are no longer fit as obligatory burnt offerings, they are offered as voluntary burnt offerings. But here, if you do not keep the אשם in its original status, is there such a thing as a voluntary אשם?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to why the אשם מצורע is different from the burnt offerings it was compared to. The burnt offerings have a 'backup' identity, but the אשם does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A burnt offering slaughtered for the wrong purpose can simply be offered as a נדבה, so it loses the special rules of its original role. An אשם has no voluntary form. So if it is to be offered at all, it must keep its original identity as an אשם מצורע, and that includes needing its נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: An obligatory burnt offering, which a person must bring
A voluntary burnt offering, given freely
A voluntary guilt offering, which does not exist
You keep it in its original status

phrases.english: If they are not fit for an obligatory burnt offering
phrases.notes: 'They' are the burnt offerings discussed just before, which were slaughtered not for their own sake.

phrases.english: they are offered as a voluntary burnt offering,
but here,
if you do not keep it in its original status,
is there such a thing as a voluntary guilt offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא חֲזוּ לְעוֹלַת חוֹבָה קׇרְבִי לְעוֹלַת נְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer, begun before this section, that defends רבי יוחנן against the comparison to burnt offerings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו should lose its original rules, the way the burnt offerings do
steps.terutzMaskana: Since no voluntary אשם exists, the אשם must keep its original identity and therefore still needs נסכים

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a flawed אשם מצורע is still offered on the altar and needs נסכים, exactly as רבי יוחנן said. The מצורע must still bring another אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught in line with רבי יוחנן: an אשם מצורע that was slaughtered not for its own sake, or whose blood was not placed on the thumbs, is still brought up on the altar and needs נסכים. But the מצורע needs another אשם to permit him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי יוחנן. This backs up his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the flawed אשם still goes on the altar and still needs נסכים, which is exactly רבי יוחנן's point. It also adds that the offering does not do its job for the owner. The מצורע has to bring a second אשם before he is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering a recovered מצורע brings as part of his purification
Slaughtered for a different purpose than the one it was set aside for
The right thumb and big toe of the מצורע
The flour and wine offerings that go along with an animal offering
In line with his opinion

steps.whatToRemember: An אשם מצורע that went wrong is still offered as an אשם with its נסכים, but it does not complete the מצורע's purification, so he must bring another one.

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with רבי יוחנן:
a leper's guilt offering that one slaughtered not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן מִדָּמוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי בְּהוֹנוֹת –
phrases.english: or where one did not put some of its blood on the thumbs,
phrases.notes: These are the right thumb and big toe of the מצורע (ויקרא 14:14).

phrases.english: it is still brought up on the altar,
and it requires libations,
and he needs another guilt offering to permit him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports, from a ברייתא, the ruling just explained in step 1
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a flawed אשם מצורע still needs נסכים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that such an אשם goes on the altar and requires נסכים

steps.title: Temple measures were filled heaped, except the כהן גדול's
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that every measuring vessel in the מקדש held its amount when filled heaped above the rim. The כהן גדול's measure was the exception: its heaped amount fit inside, level with the rim.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All the measures in the מקדש were filled heaped, except for the measure of the כהן גדול, whose heaped amount fit inside it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It describes how the measuring vessels in the מקדש were filled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the correct amount was measured by heaping the contents above the rim. The כהן גדול's vessel was built a little bigger. So the same heaped amount fit inside it when the flour was leveled off.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה
Measuring vessels
Filled heaped above the rim
The High Priest
Its heaped amount was held inside it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying the כהן גדול got less. The amount was the same; only the vessel was bigger, so the amount fit inside it level.

phrases.english: MISHNA: All the measures that were in the Temple
were filled heaped,
except for that of the High Priest,
phrases.notes: This is the vessel for measuring the flour of his daily griddle offering.

phrases.english: whose heaped amount was inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל מִדּוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ הָיוּ נִגְדָּשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Temple measures were used heaped, except the כהן גדול's measure, which held the heaped amount level

steps.title: Overflow from liquid measures is holy, overflow from dry measures is not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds that what spills over the rim of a liquid measure is holy. What spills over a dry measure is ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: For liquid measures, their overflows are holy. For dry measures, their overflows are not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second rule about the measuring vessels. This one is about the contents that spill over the edge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes a difference between liquids and dry goods. Liquid that runs over the outside of a liquid measure keeps its holiness. Dry material that falls off a dry measure stays ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: Measures for liquids, such as wine and oil
Measures for dry goods, such as flour
Their overflows, the part that spills over the edge
Holy / ordinary

steps.whatToRemember: Liquid overflow is holy; dry overflow is not.

phrases.english: Measures for liquids: their overflows are holy;
and measures for dry goods: their overflows are not holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a second rule about the measures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Overflow from liquid measures is holy; overflow from dry measures is not

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: The Vessel's Status Decides
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains the overflow rule: liquid measures are holy vessels, so their overflow is holy. Dry measures are ordinary vessels, so their overflow is ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: the liquid measuring vessels are holy, so what spills from them is holy. The dry measuring vessels are not holy, so what spills from them is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives רבי עקיבא's reason for the rule from Step 4. The overflow takes on the status of the vessel it spilled from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 stated the rule without a reason. רבי עקיבא supplies one: liquid measures were holy vessels and dry measures were not. Because of that, whatever spills over the rim takes on the vessel's status.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
The measuring vessels for liquids are holy,
therefore their overflows are holy.
The measuring vessels for dry goods are ordinary,
therefore their overflows are ordinary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a reason for the overflow rule stated in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Overflow follows the status of the vessel: a holy vessel makes holy overflow, an ordinary vessel makes ordinary overflow.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Was the Overflow Ever Inside?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי gives a different reason. Liquid overflow was once inside the vessel and got pushed out. Dry overflow never went in, because it was piled on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: that is not the reason. The real reason is that the liquid is pushed out from inside the vessel, but the dry goods are not pushed out from inside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי rejects רבי עקיבא's reason and offers his own explanation for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree on the result. They disagree only on the reason. For רבי יוסי, what counts is whether the overflow was ever inside the holy space of the vessel. Liquid that spills was inside and was pushed out, while heaped flour that falls off the top was never inside.

keyTerms.meaning: Not because of that reason
Uprooted, pushed out from where it was

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not disagree about the rule itself. Liquid overflow is still holy and dry overflow is still ordinary. He only gives a different reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
It is not because of that,
rather, it is because the liquid is pushed out
and the dry goods are not pushed out.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לֹא מִשּׁוּם זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי עקיבא's reason and gives a different one for the same rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Overflow is holy only if it was once inside the vessel and was pushed out, which happens with liquids and not with heaped dry goods.

steps.title: Whose View Says Every Measure Was Heaped?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view the משנה follows when it says all measures were heaped. Neither רבי מאיר nor the רבנן fits, because each held that a tenth-measure was leveled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If it is רבי מאיר, only one of his two measures was heaped. If it is the רבנן, their one measure was leveled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It goes back to the משנה's first rule from Step 3 and shows that it seems to fit no known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי מאיר and the רבנן argued about the tenth-measures for dry goods. For רבי מאיר there were two, one heaped and one leveled. For the רבנן there was only one, and it was leveled. Either way, not every measure was heaped, so the משנה's claim is hard to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
Heaped above the rim
Leveled, even with the rim
The Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: GEMARA: Whose opinion is this?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking about the משנה's opening line, that every measure in the מקדש was heaped.

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר – חַד גָּדוּשׁ הֲוָה,
phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir, only one was heaped,
phrases.notes: This refers to the earlier argument about the tenth-measures used for flour.

phrases.english: if it is the Rabbis, there was one, and it was leveled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the overflow discussion and goes back to the משנה's first rule from Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that all measures in the מקדש were heaped.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known opinions hold that at least one tenth-measure was leveled, so 'all heaped' fits neither.

steps.title: רב חסדא: 'All Measures' Means 'All Measurings'
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה follows רבי מאיר. 'All measures' means that every measuring done with the heaped vessel was done heaped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Really it is רבי מאיר. What does 'all measures' mean? All measurings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by rereading one word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not mean that every vessel was a heaped vessel. It means that every act of measuring with that heaped vessel was done heaped. That fits רבי מאיר, who held that one of the two tenth-measures was heaped.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really (keeping the first suggestion)
Measures, meaning the vessels
Measurings, meaning the acts of measuring

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי מאיר. 'כל מדות' is read as 'כל מדידות': all measurings, not all vessels.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Actually, it is Rabbi Meir,
and what does "all measures" mean?
All measurings.
phrases.notes: A small change in wording: not every vessel, but every time they measured with the heaped vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וּמַאי כׇּל מִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'All measures' means every vessel in the מקדש was heaped.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'All measures' means every measuring done with the heaped vessel, which fits רבי מאיר.

steps.title: What Exactly Do They Disagree About?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's overflow rule and asks what the תנאים are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Measures of liquid, their overflows are holy." What are they disagreeing about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next discussion. It asks what the real difference is between the first תנא, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three give the same result: liquid overflow is holy and dry overflow is not. So the גמרא wants to know where their different reasons would lead to a different practical outcome. The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: "Measures of liquid, their overflows are holy,"
phrases.notes: This quotes the line from the משנה in Step 4.

phrases.english: in what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the overflow rule and the reasons given in Steps 4 to 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference results from the different reasons given by the first תנא, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי.

steps.title: The first view: liquid measures were anointed inside and outside
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא holds that liquid measures were anointed on both sides, so overflow running down the outside becomes holy. Dry measures were anointed only inside, so their overflow stays ordinary.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא holds: the liquid measure was anointed both inside and outside. The dry measure was anointed only inside, not outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering its question from step 9 by explaining the reasoning of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vessels became holy by being anointed with oil, and a holy vessel makes holy what it touches. Liquid overflow runs down the outside of the vessel, so if the outside was anointed, the overflow touches a holy surface and becomes holy. Dry measures were never anointed on the outside, so their overflow touches nothing holy.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה
The measuring vessel for liquids, like wine and oil
The measuring vessel for dry items, like flour
Was anointed with oil, which made the vessel holy
On the inside / on the outside

phrases.english: The first תנא holds:
the measure for liquid was anointed,
both on the inside and on the outside;
the measure for dry items was anointed on the inside,
and was not anointed on the outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 9 by explaining the first opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference lies in where each vessel was anointed: liquid measures inside and outside, dry measures only inside.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's view: dry measures were never anointed at all
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא agrees that liquid measures were anointed inside and outside, but holds that dry measures were not anointed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: the liquid measure was anointed both inside and outside. The dry measure was not anointed at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's position, which matches his reason from step 5 that dry measures are ordinary vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, the dry measure is holy inside, so its contents become holy, and only the overflow stays ordinary. For רבי עקיבא, the dry measure was never anointed, so it is an ordinary vessel and cannot make anything holy. That is why its overflow is ordinary.

keyTerms.meaning: At all; not even a little

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא holds:
the measure for liquid was anointed
both on the inside and on the outside,

phrases.aramaic: מִדַּת יָבֵשׁ לֹא נִמְשְׁחָה כׇּל עִיקָּר.
phrases.english: the measure for dry items was not anointed at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer by giving the second opinion and contrasting it with the תנא קמא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dry measures were never anointed, so they are ordinary vessels and cannot make overflow holy.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view: both were anointed only inside
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that both kinds of measures were anointed only inside. Liquid overflow is holy because it was inside the vessel and got pushed out. Dry overflow never went inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי holds: both were anointed only inside, not outside. The reason here is that the liquid overflow was pushed out and comes from inside the vessel, but the dry overflow was never pushed out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוסי's view, which matches his reason from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, the outside of the vessel plays no role, since neither vessel was anointed outside. What matters is whether the overflow was ever inside the holy vessel. Liquid fills the vessel and then spills over, so it was inside. Dry flour is piled on top and never sat inside.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that; both of them
This is the reason
Uprooted, pushed out of its place
From inside the vessel

phrases.english: And רבי יוסי holds:
this one and that one were anointed on the inside
and were not anointed on the outside,
and here, this is the reason:
that the liquid was pushed out,
and it comes from inside the vessel,
but the dry item was not pushed out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion, which does not depend on outside anointing at all.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Neither vessel was anointed outside. Liquid overflow is holy only because it was once inside the vessel.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views: the תנא קמא says liquid measures were anointed outside too. רבי עקיבא says dry measures were never anointed. רבי יוסי says the only question is whether the overflow was ever inside the vessel.

steps.title: Challenge: the person only meant to make holy what he needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי's reason. Even if the liquid overflow was once inside the vessel, the person intended to make holy only the exact measure he needed, not the extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it was pushed out, so what? A person intends only for what he needs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given for רבי יוסי: being inside the vessel for a moment should not be enough to make the overflow holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A measuring vessel makes holy only what the person meant it to hold, which is the exact measure. The extra liquid was never part of what he wanted, so its brief time inside the vessel should not matter. This makes רבי יוסי's distinction between liquid and dry look weak.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? So what?
A man, a person
For what he needs
Intends, has in mind

phrases.english: And if it was pushed out, what of it?
A person has in mind only what he needs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given for רבי יוסי in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי's reason that liquid overflow is holy because it was once inside the vessel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel makes holy only what the person intends, which is the exact measure. Being inside the vessel briefly should not make the unwanted extra holy.

steps.title: Service vessels make things holy even without intent
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי בר שישנא, quoting רב, learns from רבי יוסי's view that כלי שרת make their contents holy even when the person did not intend it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי בר שישנא said in the name of רב: This teaches that כלי שרת make things holy even without the person's intent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 13. The overflow is holy even though the person did not mean to make it holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 argued that the person only meant to make the exact measure holy, so the extra should stay ordinary. רב answers that intent does not matter here. Anything that enters a כלי שרת becomes holy automatically, so the overflow that was inside the vessel is holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels used for the service in the בית המקדש
Make holy (what is put inside them)
Without the person's intent or awareness
This teaches us (a lesson drawn from a source)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic question: does a כלי שרת make things holy by its own power, or only when the person means it?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב דִּימִי בַּר שִׁישְׁנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Rav Dimi bar Shishna said in the name of Rav:
That is to say,
service vessels consecrate even without intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13's challenge by saying intent is not needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the underlying rule: holiness from a כלי שרת does not depend on intent.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Holiness requires intent, so the extra liquid should stay ordinary.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי שרת makes things holy even without intent, so the overflow is holy.

steps.title: Intent is needed, but the חכמים made a decree
steps.stepSummary: רבינא holds that כלי שרת need intent, so by Torah law the overflow is not holy. The חכמים still treated it as holy so people would not think holy things may be taken out of a כלי שרת back to ordinary use.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, I can tell you that כלי שרת make things holy only with intent. But the חכמים made a גזירה, so that people would not say you may take something out of a כלי שרת and make it ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different answer to step 13. He accepts that intent is needed and explains the holiness of the overflow as a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא agrees with step 13 that, by Torah law, the overflow is not holy. But onlookers saw the liquid inside a holy vessel. If it were then treated as ordinary, they might wrongly conclude that holy things can be returned to ordinary status. So the חכמים declared it holy.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (I keep my original position)
With intent
A protective rule made by the חכמים
To ordinary, non-holy status

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא does NOT say the overflow is ordinary in practice. It is treated as holy, but only because of a rabbinic גזירה, not because of Torah law.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, I will say to you,

phrases.aramaic: כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין אֶלָּא מִדַּעַת,
phrases.english: service vessels consecrate only with intent,
but it is a decree, lest people say
that one may take out from service vessels to non-sacred use.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 14 and offers a different answer to step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic decree: the law is rabbinic, not from the Torah.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either intent is not needed (step 14), or the overflow should be ordinary.
steps.terutzMaskana: Intent is needed, but the overflow is holy because of a rabbinic גזירה.

steps.title: רבי זירא quotes the case of the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא brings a source: if the לחם הפנים was set out late in the week, it must stay on the שולחן until the next שבת, even for many days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged: If the כהן arranged the bread and the frankincense bowls after שבת, and burned the frankincense on the next שבת, it is disqualified. What should he do? Leave it until the following שבת, because even if it stays on the שולחן many days, there is nothing wrong with that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is setting up a challenge to רבינא by quoting a source about the לחם הפנים. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bread must stay on the שולחן a full week, from שבת to שבת. If it was put down midweek, the כהן waits one more שבת. The point to notice is that the bread may stay in a כלי שרת longer than usual without anyone worrying about how it looks.

keyTerms.meaning: Bowls of frankincense set beside the לחם הפנים
Burned (on the מזבח)
The golden Table in the היכל, itself a כלי שרת
Disqualified

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira raised an objection:
If he arranged the bread and the bowls of frankincense
after Shabbat,
and burned the bowls of frankincense on Shabbat,
it is disqualified.
How should he proceed?
He should leave it until the following Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הוּא עַל שֻׁלְחָן יָמִים רַבִּים –
phrases.english: for even if it is on the Table many days,
there is nothing wrong with that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to attack רבינא's גזירה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's explanation that the overflow is holy only because of a גזירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: a case where the חכמים apparently did not worry about how the use of a כלי שרת might look.

steps.title: Why no decree for the לחם הפנים?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks: if the חכמים worried about misunderstandings with כלי שרת, why not forbid leaving the bread extra days, so people won't think a כלי שרת can be used for storage?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? There too, let us say there should be a גזירה, so people won't say that one may store things in כלי שרת!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי זירא states his actual challenge. The חכמים made no גזירה in the bread case, so why does רבינא assume they made one for the overflow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים feared people misreading the use of כלי שרת, the same fear applies to the bread. People might think a כלי שרת can be used to store holy food and keep it from becoming disqualified. Yet the bread is allowed to stay, which suggests the חכמים did not make such גזירות at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But why?
There too (in the other case as well)
Deposit or store

phrases.english: But why?
There too, let us say:
a decree, lest people say:
one may store things in service vessels!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the point of the source quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consistency: the same fear of misunderstanding should have led to a גזירה for the לחם הפנים, but there is none.

steps.title: Inside the היכל is different from outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cases differ. The bread is inside the היכל, where few people see. The measuring happens outside, where everyone sees, so only there was a גזירה needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you comparing inside to outside? Inside, not everyone knows what happens. Outside, everyone knows.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבינא by showing that רבי זירא's comparison does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה is made only where people might see something and draw the wrong conclusion. The לחם הפנים sits inside the היכל, where ordinary people do not see it, so there is nothing to misunderstand. The measuring of liquids happens outside in public view, so a גזירה is needed there, and רבינא's explanation stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Inside (the היכל)
Outside (the היכל)
You are setting one case against another
Everyone knows (it is public)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, a כלי שרת makes things holy only with intent. The overflow is holy only by a rabbinic גזירה, which applies to public actions outside the היכל, not to private ones inside it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general rule about גזירות: the חכמים worry about public misunderstanding only where the public can actually see.

phrases.english: Are you raising a contradiction between inside and outside?!
Inside, not everyone knows what happens;
outside, everyone knows.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's challenge by showing the two cases differ.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (public outside versus hidden inside).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bread case shows the חכמים made no גזירות about כלי שרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גזירה is needed only where the public sees, so רבינא's גזירה outside still stands.

steps.title: A משנה about the leftover libations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from שקלים: the מוֹתַר נְסָכִים are used for קֵיץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: the leftover נְסָכִים go toward קֵיץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that connects to the overflow discussion. It is setting up a question about what this משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something called מוֹתַר נְסָכִים, 'leftover libations,' is used to buy extra offerings for the מזבח. The משנה does not say what kind of leftover it means. That gap will lead to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftover or extra from the libations
Wine-offerings (and their flour and oil) brought with קרבנות
Extra עולות offered when the מזבח would otherwise be idle

phrases.english: We learned there, in a משנה:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a משנה in מסכת שקלים.

phrases.english: The surplus libations go to the supplementary offerings of the altar.
phrases.notes: קיץ literally means 'summer fruit,' like dessert for the מזבח. These are extra offerings brought when nothing else is being offered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the overflow of measuring vessels to a משנה about what happens to leftover libations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Surplus libations are used to fund קֵיץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.

steps.title: What counts as surplus libations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by מוֹתַר נְסָכִים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'surplus libations'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to define the term in the משנה. It is setting up two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. The גמרא just wants to know what leftover the משנה is talking about, because 'leftover' could mean several things.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asks for a definition)

phrases.english: What is 'surplus libations'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of 'leftover' the term מוֹתַר נְסָכִים refers to.

steps.title: First answer: the overflow of the measuring vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף says מוֹתַר נְסָכִים means the overflow that spills from the measuring vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף says: it is the overflow of the measuring vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר יוסף gives the first definition. The 'leftover' is what spills over the top when the liquids are measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties straight back to the overflow discussed earlier, where the measuring vessels are כלי שרת. In his view, that overflow is not used for the original offering. Instead it goes to קֵיץ הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.

keyTerms.meaning: The overflow of the measuring vessels

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef says:
The overflows of the measuring vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר: בֵּירוּצֵי מִדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of what מוֹתַר נְסָכִים means.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוֹתַר נְסָכִים is the liquid that overflows the measuring vessels.

steps.title: Second answer: the flour supplier's fixed price
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן links מוֹתַר נְסָכִים to a different משנה. There, a supplier promised flour at four סאה per סלע, and the price rose to three, but he must still supply four.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: it is like what we learned. Someone agreed to supply fine flour at four סאה for a סלע, and the price went to three. He must still supply at four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different definition. He points to a case about a supplier who sells flour to the Temple at a fixed price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה, the supplier must keep his deal even after the market price goes up, so the Temple gets more flour than its money would now buy. רבי יוחנן says מוֹתַר נְסָכִים is like this case, not the spill from the measuring cups. The גמרא will go on to explain exactly how this case connects to the surplus.

keyTerms.meaning: One who takes on the job of supplying
Fine flour
A measure of volume
A coin (the price unit here)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Stood at three' means the price went UP. A סלע now buys only three סאה instead of four. Fewer סאה per coin means flour is more expensive.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Like that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This is another משנה in מסכת שקלים.

phrases.english: One who accepts upon himself to supply fine flour at four
phrases.notes: He means four סאה of flour for one סלע coin.

phrases.english: and the price stood at three,
he must supply at four,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, competing answer to the question, disagreeing with רבי חייא בר יוסף.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוֹתַר נְסָכִים is like the case of a supplier bound to his old, cheaper price after the market price rises.
